mutations.after: // mutated: the preview frame no longer carries the brief's template
mutations.because: The template is the only thing that carries an html layer and its elements into the composite request. Drop it and `resolveLayerList` falls back to the image-text canonical list, so the preview draws a shade, an accent and a message the brief never asked for — the element the operator just typed is edited on screen and simply is not there. That is D45's fabrication failure wearing the preview's coat: an editor that shows a creative the run would not produce.

HL3's drawer is the canvas half of HL-D5 and the only half the editor preview can show (HL-D7: user markup is never rendered into the operator's DOM). A drawer that returns before painting leaves the route answering 200 image/png for a cell whose element list is invisible — the preview's own promise, broken in the one place a user would look to notice. The bytes still decode, the cache key still moves; only the pixels can tell.

mutations.after: // mutated: a disabled layer is no longer skipped on the still path
mutations.because: X9's promise is that a disabled layer renders exactly what the template renders with that layer absent — the toggle the editor exposes must mean what it says on the still frame the preview draws. Remove the skip and switching an html layer off leaves its elements painted: the operator hides a layer and the preview keeps showing it, so the one control that answers "is this in the creative" lies.
